text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a correlated spike in preemptible interruptions across us-west2-a/b for A100 pools starting ~09:10 UTC. latency p95 for infer clusters jumped ~180ms.

maria: saw it too, graphs look like interruptions clustered by instance-family (a2-highgpu vs a2-megagpu) not just AZ.

devon: Ops alert fired: `spot-interrupt-rate` threshold breached for >3 groups. raw interruption events: 84 in 12m.

ops-bot: ALERT: spot-interrupt-rate (severity:warning) — 84 events in 12m in cluster=redwood-infer-us-west2. Ticket created - INFRA-4821. :rotating_light:

alex: quick dump of the prom query i used:

```
sum by(zone, instance_family) (increase(gcp_preemptible_interruptions_total[12m]))
/ sum by(zone, instance_family) (increase(gcp_preemptible_allocations_total[12m]))
```

alex: output shows two instance_family cohorts with >0.18 interruption ratio.

sophie: is this price-driven (spot reclaim due to capacity) or maintenance? any provider maintenance notices?

maria: checked provider events, nothing scheduled. also price history for those families spiked 15m prior. looks like capacity pressure.

devon: hypothesis: short-lived blips of reclaim across related host pools — causes KV-cache churn and tail latency. SLO regression math: small interrupt bursts = high task restart rate -> bump in p95.

alex: proposal: cohort signals by (zone, instance_family, node_image) and compute a composite "eviction_score" so alerts can be less noisy and more actionable. eviction_score = weighted(sum(interrupt_rate), recent_price_delta, pool_util_variance).

maria: agree. we should also tie alerts to SLO impact not just raw interrupts. e.g. alert only when interruption_score > 0.15 AND estimated_slo_loss > 0.1% over 30m.

devon: adding a PromQL sketch for eviction_score panel:

```
(eviction_events_ratio * 0.6) + (clamp_max(price_delta_pct,0.2) * 0.3) + (pool_util_variance_norm * 0.1)
```

sophie: nice. also we should add a short-circuit mitigation in autoscaler: when cohort_eviction_score > 0.2 => trigger hedging policy (kick new allocations in dedicated/ondemand pool and throttle new spot accepts).

maria: cost tradeoff: hedging with dedicated adds ~35% cost for affected jobs but reduces SLO penalty. we should compute burn vs risk. can automate with simple expected_cost_of_slo = sla_penalty_usd * prob_failure_estimate.

alex: action items:
- (alex) implement cohorting labels in spot-sensor job and update dashboard panels.
- (devon) create new Prometheus rule for eviction_score and a composite alert that references estimated_slo_loss.
- (maria) run backtest on last 90d to estimate hedging cost vs SLO savings.

devon: i'll raise a PR for the alert defs, targetting canary for a week.

ops-bot: INFRA-4821 updated: devon assigned, priority P2, add logs and dashboard links.

maria: one more ask — add a short-lived blue-green fallback for long-running inferences (checkpoint every 60s) so restarts don't lose much work. this reduces effective SLO impact for spot faults.

alex: agreed. i'll draft the checkpoint lib spec and share in #eng-ml.

sophie: timeline? want this in place before next expected black-friday auto-scale test (2 weeks).

alex: timeline sounds reasonable. i'll aim to have cohort labels + dashboard by EOD tomorrow, devon will have alert rule in 3 days, mari­a will have analysis in 5 days.

devon: noting for the runbook: when cohort_eviction_score > 0.2 — mute noisy per-node alerts, scale hedged dedicated nodes up to 20% of pool, and open a postmortem ticket if estimated_slo_loss > 0.5%.

maria: thanks — tagging @sre for visibility. :eyes:

ops-bot: Note: automated farkle-run (spot-health-check) executed at 09:30 UTC; results attached to INFRA-4821.
